raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Italian Dressing
raw_recipe.description: This creamy Italian dressing is an easy blend of mayo, red wine vinegar, and Italian seasoning, making it a fabulous complement to any green salad.
raw_recipe.name: Creamy Italian Dressing

recipeInstructions.text: Blend mayonnaise, onion, vinegar, sugar, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt, and pepper in a blender until smooth.

review.reviewBody: Hi, all. I'm the Cathy who submitted this recipe, and I'm glad to be able to share it with those of you who have been enjoying it. It is still my favorite dressing. I just wanted to step back in and make a few comments for those who weren't satisfied. It was mentioned that the dressing tastes like biting into a plain onion, and that it was hot, and another used a red onion and not all the sugar. You will notice the onion ingredient says "1/2 a SMALL onion". This would be approximately 1/2 cup chopped, and please do use a mild white onion. The hot onion definitely makes the dressing hot and bitter. The kind of onion used will affect the flavor of the dressing. Another used just garlic salt and recommended not to use the extra salt. The recipe doesn't call for garlic salt but garlic powder, which has no salt in it. Yet another didn't use the onion at all, only an Italian seasoning packet. In my opinion, to write a review on a recipe requires you follow the recipe as written and not make substitutions, otherwise you are writing a review on the recipe as you changed it. I hope you continue to enjoy this fabulous dressing, and for those who didn't enjoy it, you might give it another chance using the instructions as written. Then if you don't like it, you'll be entirely justified in your opinion! Happy eating!

I've made this three times now, and I absolutely love it. I tweaked it a bit by cutting the sugar back to two teaspoons and substituting 1/2 teaspoon of onion powder for the small onion. So far I've used it on garden salad, and as an addition to my bean salad. It's too thick to pour out of a cruet, so I store and serve it in a small Pyrex covered dish. Also, if you use onion powder, you don't have to dirty a blender. Just whip it up with a wire whisk. So quick and easy to make. And, a little goes a long way. A definite keeper. Thank you, Cathy, for sharing such a great recipe!

This was a keeper. My husbands exact words "This was AMAZING!" I made a few changes or should I say added. I added a little minced garlic for a bit more texture and garlic flavor, we are a huge garlic lovin' family. I was all out of fresh onion so I used dried minced onion and soaked it in the red vinegar to dehydrate the onion. Added a splash of white vinegar and about a teaspoon more of red wine vinegar. That was all and then I stuck it in the fridge to meld. Plan on using the dressing for chicken bow tie pasta salad. Which I might try adding some grated parmasan to the dressing. But this was a great recipe. I also didn't blend it. I just mixed it with a spoon until well mixed. I am not into cleaning up extra dishes.

I was looking for light marinade for grilled chicken. I came across this recipe and made it. It was delicious. It didn't over power the chicken, it just complimented it really well. 

I didn't have any Italian seasoning so I used a teaspoon of dried oregano and a teaspoon of dried basil and two tablespoons of fresh parsley. I also used minced garlic rather then garlic powder. I can't wait to make this again.

This was really good and easy to make. I followed almost exactly except I used onion powder instead of an onion and added 1/4 tsp Stevia powder instead of sugar, and a few shakes of Parmesan cheese because I like it.

Love it!! The only change I made was I omitted the garlic powder and used a fresh clove of garlic. Letting it refrigerate overnight really makes a big difference as it does allow the flavors to blend. No more store bought for my family! I’m afraid I would have a riot on my hands!

I loved this dressing! I made a half recipe and didn't feel like taking out my mini processor so I just mixed it all in a small bowl, and chopped the onions finely. So much better than the store-bought stuff and so easy to make. Thanks Cathy...this is a keeper! UPDATE 10/21/15: Added parmesan cheese, and it's even better! Pretty close to one I really like in an Italian restaurant in Boston's North End, too. UPDATE: Used finely chopped green onions; I like a reviewer's idea of using this as a vegetable dip, too.

I loved this, but because I made a change (a necessary one, IMHO), I didn’t give it five stars. I made it as directed, but reduced the sugar to one teaspoon. I started with one, intending to add more if it needed it, but it was just perfect without the extra two teaspoons of sugar. The flavors really pop. We used the whole recipe on 6 dinner salads.

I LOVE THIS DRESSING! I am on a low carb diet so I used full fat mayo and stevia instead of the sugar. This is by far our favorite dressing! We especially love to put it on top of a healthy green salad with some cut rotiserie chicken and chopped eggs added! This is our go to dressing!! kudos!!!

It was good, but really- for us, too thick. I added 4 Tablespoons of milk & the consistency was better.
I also added 2 Tablespoons of fresh Parsley. This cut down the richness and brought a brighter flavor to it.
I will definitely make this recipe again with the minor adjustments I made.
Thankyou!
I used 1/2 teaspoon of onion powder in place of the onion and whisked it as others suggested. Thank you for sharing Cathy! It’s a favorite for me!
I was looking for a quick recipe to use on pasta salad and came across this one. I had everything on hand to make it which normally doesn’t happen! Only thing I would change is doubling the recipe!
great as is. very good with cheese in salad
As i stated in my comment below, this recipe was fantastic! Thank you!
Holy wow this is delicious! Thank you for such a delicious recipe Cathy!
Comes together easily and the flavor and consistency are excellent - definitely a keeper. On a side note I don't use a blender but the food processor was perfect for the job!
Really good. Trying to avoid seed oils as much as possible, so will try next time with buttermilk and sour cream
I made this exact and used it on a bag of chopped 'super blend' veggies. The dressing has an addictive flavor. Mixed in, it was not pegged as Italian, but definitely a zesty creamy keeper!
I made the recipe exactly as written, and my family raved about it. This was unanimously everyone's favorite salad dressing by far!

Love this! I put a little less than a tablespoon of sugar and I use a little onion powder in place of the onion, whisk it all together and it's delicious! This is the only recipe I use for creamy italian. So good!
